U1.expr: [choice(data['e1']['units']['ambig']['units'], data['e1']['units']['ambig']['w']) for k in range(9)] + [choice(data['e1']['units']['unambig']['units'], data['e1']['units']['unambig']['w']) for k in range(9)] + [choice(data['e1']['units']['complex_pair']['units'], data['e1']['units']['complex_pair']['w']) for k in range(12)] + [choice(data['e1']['units']['simple_c_pair']['units'], data['e1']['units']['simple_c_pair']['w']) for k in range(6)] + [choice(data['e1']['units']['simple_d_pair']['units'], data['e1']['units']['simple_d_pair']['w']) for k in range(6)]

T1.expr: permutation([{'imptype': t['imptype'], 'message': t['message'], 'img': [t['objs'][q[k]] for k in range(3)], 'lab': [t['labels'][q[k]] for k in range(3)]} for u, q in zip(U1, Q1) for t in u])

U2.expr: [choice(data['e2']['units']['simple_c_pair']['units'], data['e2']['units']['simple_c_pair']['w']) for k in range(6)] + [choice(data['e2']['units']['simple_d_pair']['units'], data['e2']['units']['simple_d_pair']['w']) for k in range(6)] + [choice(data['e2']['units']['complex_pair']['units'], data['e2']['units']['complex_pair']['w']) for k in range(12)] + [choice(data['e2']['units']['ambiguous']['units'], data['e2']['units']['ambiguous']['w']) for k in range(9)] + [choice(data['e2']['units']['unambiguous']['units'], data['e2']['units']['unambiguous']['w']) for k in range(9)]

targets.no_uncertainty: only rounded percentages are printed (Fig. 2/3 bootstrapped CIs are graphical)
targets.condition_note: four games as in the authors' redimptype. Exp. 1: simple 12, complex 12, ambiguous = 9 baseline fillers, unambiguous = 9 baseline + 24 display-reuse fillers (33): prior_extraction_E10.Rmd l. 44 ('all grids used in "simple" and "complex" are also used in "unamb" ... the exact same number of times'), Monster-data_E10.R l. 37, 79 (four levels). Exp. 2 (production): unambiguous = 9 baseline + simple_c + complex_d (27), ambiguous = 9 baseline + simple_d (15): simple_d's 'target' label is a coin flip between two unique true messages, so with it in 'unambiguous' an error-free population caps at (27 + 3)/33 = .909 target and .091 competitor, which cannot give the printed 96% / 1%; with 27 trials an error-free speaker scores 27/27 = 1.0 and 96% / 1% leaves 3% for distractors. Other readings in 'readings'

keyed.why: answers that make the paper's pattern true: never a distractor; the target on simple, complex and unambiguous trials; on Exp. 1 ambiguous trials the target unless it is on the left (position effect). Exp. 2: on ambiguous AND simple_d trials the speaker sends the species message (v*) - a preference a real speaker can have; on simple_d the 'target' label is a coin flip between the two true messages, so this splits simple_d about 50/50 between 'target' and 'competitor' exactly as a real population would, and the scored unambiguous set (27 trials) gets target 1.0 (printed 96%); the earlier keyed rule picked the 'target' label on simple_d, which no participant can see, and hid the 33-trial cap (fidelity review 2)
